title: Seeing Through the Chain: Mitigate Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Models via CoT Compression and Contrastive Preference Optimization

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the attention weight distribution between visual and textual tokens, and utilizing hallucination-inducing mechanisms (like masking visual inputs) to measure the model's over-reliance on learned linguistic associations rather than grounded visual evidence.

Using the 'popular' sampling setting of the POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) benchmark, which involves yes/no queries about statistically frequent object categories to test if the model hallucinates them based on their common occurrence in training data.
